successCriteria.description: The AuditAction enum in src/shared/types/index.ts exposes a CANCEL member whose value is the string literal 'CANCEL', appended after REJECT in the existing member order (CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT, CANCEL).

The existing AuditAction test in tests/unit/shared/types.test.ts is extended so Object.values(AuditAction) equals ['CREATE','UPDATE','DELETE','APPROVE','REJECT','CANCEL'], and the test description reflects the new member.
The project typechecks and the full Jest suite passes (npm run build && npx jest) with no non-exhaustive-switch or other type errors introduced by the new enum member.

constraints: The CANCEL member must use the string-literal value 'CANCEL' (uppercase), matching the existing AuditAction member style; do NOT reuse UPDATE or DELETE as the value.
Append CANCEL after REJECT; do not reorder or rename the existing CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT members.
No new modules, routes, service logic, or database changes; the change is limited to the shared enum definition and its unit test.
outOfScope: Any production consumer changes (audit.service.ts, audit.model.ts, leave.service.ts) — Object.values(AuditAction).includes(...) validation and value-only references already accept the new member without modification.
Adding exhaustive switch handling for CANCEL — no switch statements over AuditAction exist in the codebase, so none need updating.
Any persistence, migration, or audit-log write logic that actually records a CANCEL action — this phase only adds the enum member and its test.

entityInvariants.invariant: AuditAction is a string-literal enum whose members are the canonical persisted audit-action values; it must contain exactly CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, REJECT, CANCEL in that order, each with an uppercase string-literal value equal to its member name.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The new CANCEL member must match the existing string-literal member style (uppercase value equal to member name) of the AuditAction enum.
The updated test must extend the existing AuditAction member-list assertion in the shared enum test file rather than introducing a divergent assertion style.
